```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

# Question
if you repeatedly sample from skewed distributions, how often does a nominal 95% confidence interval for the mean actually contain the true mean, and how does that change with sample size?

# Initial guess:

* For skewed distributions the interval most of the time still contains the true mean [10.28.2026;13:09]

# Distributions:

* **Normal**(Symmetric)

$$f(x) = \frac{1}{\sigma\sqrt{2\pi}}e^{-\frac{(x-\mu)^2}{2\sigma^2}}\qquad f(x)\sim N(\mu,\sigma^2)$$

* **$\chi^2$-distribution**(Skewed)

$$g(x) = \frac{x^{k/2-1}e^{-x/2}}{2^{k/2}\Gamma(k/2)}\qquad g(x)\sim\chi^2(k)$$
# SEED: 
```{r}
set.seed(67)
```


# Samples

## normal
```{r}
l_norm_samp <- rnorm(10000,12,sqrt(24))
s_norm_samp <- rnorm(30,12,sqrt(24))
```

## $\chi^2$
```{r}
l_chi_samp <- rchisq(10000,12)
s_chi_samp <- rchisq(30,12)
```


# checks
## normal
### large
```{r}
cat("length:", length(l_norm_samp),"\n")
cat("mean:", mean( l_norm_samp),"\n")
cat("variance:", var(l_norm_samp))

hist(l_norm_samp,
     col = "lightsalmon",
     main = "Normal distribution with large sample",
     ylim = c(0,2000))
abline(v = mean( l_norm_samp), col = "slateblue", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
text(x = mean(l_norm_samp) , y = 2000, labels = paste("Mean =", round(mean(l_norm_samp), 2)), col = "darkgreen")
abline(v = 12, col = "yellow", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
text(x = 12 , y = 1850, labels = paste("Set Mean =", 12), col = "black")
```

### small
```{r}
cat("length:", length(s_norm_samp),"\n")
cat("mean:", mean( s_norm_samp),"\n")
cat("variance:", var(s_norm_samp))

hist(s_norm_samp,
     col = "tomato",
     main = "Normal distribution with small sample",
     ylim = c(0,10))
abline(v = mean( s_norm_samp), col = "darkblue", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
text(x = mean(s_norm_samp)+9 , y = 10, labels = paste("Mean =", round(mean(s_norm_samp), 2)), col = "springgreen4")
abline(v = 12, col = "yellow", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
text(x = 0 , y = 8, labels = paste("Set Mean =", 12), col = "black")
```

## $\chi^2$
### large
```{r}
h   <- hist(l_chi_samp, plot = FALSE)
top <- max(h$counts) * 1.15            # headroom above the tallest bar

plot(h,
     col  = "lightblue",
     main = "Chi-square distribution with large sample",
     ylim = c(0, top))
abline(v = mean(l_chi_samp), col = "firebrick1", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
abline(v = 12, col = "yellow", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
text(x = mean(l_chi_samp), y = top, pos = 4,
     labels = paste("Mean =", round(mean(l_chi_samp), 2)), col = "darkmagenta")
text(x = 12, y = top * 0.93, pos = 2,
     labels = paste("Set Mean =", 12), col = "black")

```

### small
```{r}
cat("length:", length(s_chi_samp),"\n")
cat("mean:", mean( s_chi_samp),"\n")
cat("variance:", var(s_chi_samp))

hist(s_chi_samp,
     col = "steelblue1",
     main = "Chi-square distribution with small sample",
     ylim = c(0,10))
abline(v = mean( s_chi_samp), col = "red2", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
text(x = mean(s_chi_samp)+2 , y = 10, labels = paste("Mean =", round(mean(s_chi_samp), 2)), col = "purple")
abline(v = 12, col = "yellow", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
text(x = 9.85 , y = 8.5, labels = paste("Set Mean =", 12), col = "black")
```

```{r}
# several small samples: each column is one sample of size n_small
n_small <- 30
reps    <- 4

s_norm_mat <- replicate(reps, rnorm(n_small, 12, sqrt(24)))
s_chi_mat  <- replicate(reps, rchisq(n_small, 12))

dim(s_norm_mat); dim(s_chi_mat)          # check against your prediction
colMeans(s_norm_mat); apply(s_norm_mat, 2, var)
colMeans(s_chi_mat);  apply(s_chi_mat, 2, var)
```


```{r}
# large samples, side by side, same x-axis
xr <- range(l_norm_samp, l_chi_samp)
op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
hist(l_norm_samp, xlim = xr, main = "Normal, large")
abline(v = 12, lwd = 2, lty = 2)
hist(l_chi_samp,  xlim = xr, main = "Chi-square, large")
abline(v = 12, lwd = 2, lty = 2)
par(op)
```


```{r}
# small samples: top row normal, bottom row chi-square
xr_s <- range(s_norm_mat, s_chi_mat)
op <- par(mfrow = c(2, reps))
for (j in 1:reps) { hist(s_norm_mat[, j], xlim = xr_s, main = paste("Normal, draw", j)); abline(v = 12, lwd = 2, lty = 2) }
for (j in 1:reps) { hist(s_chi_mat[, j],  xlim = xr_s, main = paste("Chi-sq, draw", j));  abline(v = 12, lwd = 2, lty = 2) }
par(op)
```
